title: Models and Methods to Evaluate Transport of Drug Delivery Systems Across Cellular Barriers
protocol: Place 0.8 mm pore PET transwell inserts into a 24-well plate.
Dilute human epithelial colorectal adenocarcinoma (Caco-2) cells in DMEM medium supplemented with 15% fetal bovine serum and 1% Pen Strep.
Add 200-400 μl of the cell solution into the upper chamber of each transwell insert, at a density of 1.5 x 10^5 cells/cm^2.
Fill the lower (basolateral) chamber with 700 - 900 μl of DMEM medium supplemented with 15% fetal bovine serum and 1% Pen Strep.
Culture cells at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% humidity for 16-21 days.
Replace the medium in the upper and lower chamber every 3-4 days using indicated volumes.
Aspirate the medium from the lower chamber.
Aspirate the medium from the upper chamber.
Fill the upper chamber with fresh medium.
Fill the lower chamber with fresh medium.
Submerge STX100 electrodes in an electrolyte solution for short-term storage (less than 2 weeks).
Connect the electrode cable to the EVOM volt-ohm meter to maintain internal short-circuit and symmetry.
Rinse the electrodes in a sterile electrolyte solution before each resistance measurement.
With the volt-ohm meter set to resistance, place electrodes vertically in a well containing the transwell insert.
Position the short electrode in the upper chamber and the long electrode in the lower chamber touching the bottom of the well.
Record the resistance value once the reading stabilizes.
Calculate resistivity by subtracting background resistance and multiplying by membrane surface area.
Repeat measurements every 1-2 days until TEER values plateau, typically taking 2-3 weeks from cell plating.
For verification of tight junctions in high TEER monolayers, fix cells with cold 2% paraformaldehyde for 15 min.
Wash cells with PBS and incubate with 1 μg/ml anti-occludin for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash cells again with PBS and incubate with 7.5 μg/ml fluorescently-labeled secondary antibodies for 30 min at room temperature.
Use wells with low TEER as a negative control for barrier formation.
Couple labeled targeting antibody to the surface of NCs.
Incubate polystyrene nanobeads for 1 hour at room temperature with 125I-anti-ICAM.
Centrifuge at 13,000 x g for 3 minutes.
Remove non-coated counterparts in the supernatant by aspiration.
Resuspend the pellet containing coated NCs using 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS by pipetting.
Sonicate the resuspended particles at low power to disrupt potential particle aggregates.
Measure size, polydispersity, and ζ-potential of coated particles using dynamic light scattering.
Quantify the number of 125I-labeled targeting antibody molecules on the particle surface using a gamma counter.
Add 125I-antibody NCs (e.g., 125I-anti-ICAM NCs; 56 nCi/ml) to the upper chamber above confluent Caco-2 monolayers with TEER ≥350 Ω×cm².
Incubate at 37 °C for one or more desired time intervals.
Collect medium from the upper and lower chambers for measurement.
Wash the upper chamber once with 0.5 ml DMEM at 37 °C.
Wash the lower chamber once with 1 ml dH2O.
Incubate permeable filters in a gamma counter tube with 1% Triton X-100 for 10 min.
Measure total radioactivity of washes using a gamma counter.
Mix 300 μl sample (from upper, lower, or cell fractions) with 700 μl of 3% BSA in PBS and 200 μl trichloroacetic acid (TCA).
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 15 min.
Centrifuge TCA samples at 3,000 x g for 5 min to separate intact protein from degraded protein or 125I fraction.
Measure radioactivity of free 125I fraction in supernatant.
Subtract free 125I radioactivity from total radioactivity measured before centrifugation.
Culture Caco-2 monolayers on transwell inserts.
Add 125I-albumin alone to the upper chamber medium above the cell monolayer (negative control).
Incubate at 37 °C for the selected time interval(s).
Measure TEER before, during, and after incubation.
Collect all fractions for total 125I and free 125I measurements.
Add non-radiolabeled antibody-targeted NCs to the upper chamber medium along with 125I-albumin.
Incubate at 37 °C for the selected time interval(s).
Measure TEER before, during, and after incubation.
Collect all fractions for total 125I and free 125I measurements.
Add cell media containing 5 mM H2O2 to the upper and lower chambers of the transwell insert.
Incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.
Measure TEER (Section 2.3) before adding 125I-albumin.
Add 125I-albumin to the upper chamber after H2O2 treatment.
Measure TEER at various time points throughout the incubation to identify TEER value decay caused by H2O2-induced opening of the cell junctions.
Incubate confluent Caco-2 monolayers with 50 μM monodansylcadaverine (MDC).
Incubate confluent Caco-2 monolayers with 1 μg/ml filipin.
Incubate confluent Caco-2 monolayers with 0.5 μM wortmannin.
Incubate confluent Caco-2 monolayers with 20 μM [5-(N-ethyl-N-isopropyl) amiloride] (EIPA).
Use 125I-IgG NCs as a negative control for inhibitor effects.
Use 125I-albumin as a negative control for inhibitor effects.
Measure TEER before incubation with inhibitors and radiolabeled materials.
Measure TEER during incubation with inhibitors and radiolabeled materials.
Measure TEER after incubation with inhibitors and radiolabeled materials.
